title: Comparing Human Role-Players and LLM-Simulated Clients in Online Counselling Training: An Analysis of Counselling Patterns
abstract: arXiv:2610.40563v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This study investigates the capabilities of Large Language Models to simulate counselling clients in educational role-plays in comparison to human role-players. Initially, we recorded role-playing sessions, where novice counsellors interacted with human peers acting as clients, followed by role-plays between humans and clients simulated by Mistrals Mixtral 8x7b using 4-bit quantization. These interactions were analysed with a counselling communication pattern system at sentence level. We investigated two key questions: (1) to what extent LLM-generated responses replicate authentic conversational dynamics and (2) whether counsellors' communication behaviour differs when interacting with human versus LLM-simulated clients. translated_title: 在线心理咨询训练中人类角色扮演者与大语言模型模拟来访者的比较：咨询模式分析
translated_abstract: 本研究调查了大语言模型在教育性角色扮演中模拟心理咨询来访者的能力，并与人类角色扮演者进行比较。首先，我们记录了新手咨询师与扮演来访者的人类同伴互动的角色扮演场景，随后进行了人类与由Mistral的Mixtral 8x7b模型（采用4位量化）模拟的来访者之间的角色扮演。这些互动在句子层面使用心理咨询沟通模式系统进行分析。我们研究了两个关键问题：（1）大语言模型生成的回复在多大程度上能复制真实的对话动态；（2）咨询师在与人类来访者和与LLM模拟来访者互动时，其沟通行为是否存在差异。研究结果突出了两种场景下咨询模式应用的相似性与差异性，显示了基于LLM的角色扮演练习在提升咨询能力方面的潜力。
tldr: 本研究通过句子级心理咨询沟通模式分析发现，大语言模型模拟来访者与人类角色扮演者相比在对话模式上既有相似性也有差异性，表明基于LLM的角色扮演练习有潜力用于提升心理咨询师的培训效果。
en_tdlr: This study analyzes counselling communication patterns at the sentence level and finds that LLM-simulated clients exhibit both similarities and differences compared to human role-players, demonstrating the potential of LLM-based role-playing exercises to enhance counsellor training competencies.
